tags: A straight-down flight with live telemetry
A survey that draws itself as you scroll
features: The first screen flies straight down with live telemetry, so it reads as surveyors, not hobby pilots
Each service draws itself over an aerial photo as you scroll, showing exactly what the client gets handed
The price sits beside every survey, so the call starts with the job rather than the cost
A quote form that starts with the postcode and gives back a job reference and a flight log
name: Overhead
short: A drone survey website where each service is a survey you watch draw itself.
long: Overhead's homepage flies straight down over a Peak District field with live telemetry. Scroll on and a pinned aerial photo draws each survey in turn, roof defects, cut and spoil, contours and a film circuit, with the price beside it. The quote form starts with the postcode and gives back a job reference.
proves: A survey firm can show what it hands over, not just a gallery of aerial photos.
story: Drone operators all show the same thing: pretty aerial photographs. What they are paid for is measurement, so the page draws the survey over the photo, the way the client will see it.
